text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- India Prime Minister H D Deve Gowda's 10-month-old coalition is in danger after Congress withdraws support and stakes a claim to the government.

- Malaysia welcomes Singapore's "positive move" to restore bilateral relations although it will take time for the relationship to return to its previous level after Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's remarks on Johor.
- A grenade attack kills 12 people and injures more than 100 others during an anti-government protest in Phnom Penh in front of Cambodia's National Assembly.

- Rear-Admiral Teo Chee Hean assures Singaporeans that students applying for entry to local universities will not be deprived of places if they meet the qualification despite the revision of university fees.
- Parti Islam demonstrators in Malaysia protested a cricket match between Gibraltar and Israel, but found themselves at the wrong place after organisers switched the venue of the game.
- The 150 Singapore companies who have announced their corporate results are seen posting double-digit growth despite the poor economic atmosphere last year.
- Tibs Holdings, which announced a Singapore $5.1 million loss last year, is exploring the possibility of raising bus fares to improve its revenue take.
- U.S. Treasury bond yields may trend higher while stocks may dip over signs the U.S. economy is continuing to expand.
- Malaysian Airline System Bhd plans to raise Malaysian $3.27 billion in a capital restructuring programme to help pay for the purchase of new planes and to invest in a new airport.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Singapore's regional carrier Silkair is buying a dozen planes worth US$400 million and is deciding between Boeing and Airbus as its supplier.
- Bank Negara's move to curb excessive lending for shares and high-end properties may dampen sentiment in the Malaysian share market.
- Indian stocks plunge due to political uncertainty after the Congress Party launched a bid for power by withdrawing its support of Prime Minister HD Deve Gowda's fragile minority government.
- Performance Motors gets more than 300 orders in a week after it introduced a scheme which allows ownership of a Singapore $153,000 BMW 316iA for a monthly payment of just under S$1,000 a month.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin is ready to offer Taiwan's leader the post of Vice-President in the national leadership if the island is peacefully reunited with the mainland, Kyodo news agency said.
- Tat Lee Bank's 1996 net profit rose 13.37 percent to Singapore $68.87 million, helped by a stronger performance in the second half of last year.
- Malaysia's Rashid Hussain Bhd said it has abandoned a plan to buy a 33 percent stake in a Thai brokerage to be set up by Kring Thai Finance and Securities Plc.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
